items.discussion: docs-47 (Order 47); K26's scope named the site, the playground, the book and vilan/examples, not `vilan init`'s templates
items.title: `vilan init`'s two UI templates — `crates/vilan-cli/templates/browser/counter.vl` and `templates/fullstack/src/client.vl` — still build their counter with `view("section").child(view("h1").text(..))` chains: the first UI a new user reads is the one spelling the book now writes only where a tree's shape is not fixed
items.body:
After K26 the book (Building UI's "Markup or chain"), the examples and the site write a fixed-shape tree as element syntax; the templates are the one first-contact surface left on the chain. Each is four lines (`

"hello from Vilan"

{count.derive(..)}

`). Readers to move with them: `src/init.rs` embeds both by `include_str!`; `style_chain_order.rs` lists both files as style sources (the style chains themselves are unaffected); `tests/init.rs` builds the generated projects and asserts nothing on the view chain's text. Expect `vilan check` on a fresh project to cost about +0.15% per text child (K26's router measurement). Sizing S; vilan-cli.

items.title:
a hole in element syntax that holds a non-text value — `

{count}

` over a `SignalCell`, `

{5}

` — is refused "'SignalCell' does not implement trait 'Slot', required by a generic bound of this call", spanned on the ELEMENT's `<` (not the hole) with a secondary label on std's `fun child`, a call the author never wrote; no steer to the text form (`{count.derive(\|n\| i"{n}")}`, `i"{5}"`)
items.body: Element syntax lowers `{expr}` to `.child(expr)` before analysis, so the bound failure is reported as a call-site bound failure of the desugared chain. Two improvements, either alone useful: (1) span the refusal on the hole's expression (the desugar knows it); (2) when the refused type is a number, a bool, or a `Source` of one, say that a hole takes a View, a str, a List<View> or a Source of one, and offer the i-string / `.derive(|n| i"{n}")` rewrite. The same refusal on an explicit `.child(5)` can keep today's wording. Repros: finds/hole_not_a_slot_signal.vl, finds/hole_not_a_slot_literal.vl (both 0.44.0 / next @b94cb47f). Sizing S; analyzer (the bound-failure reporter) or the element desugar's span.

items.title:
a fragment where ONE view is wanted — `fun pair(): View { <>

"a"

"b"

}` — is refused with the plain mismatch "Expected View, but got List instead"; the book promises "a type error that says so", and nothing in it says fragment or how to fix it
items.body:
A fragment lowers to a list literal, so the mismatch is accurate but reads as if the author wrote a list. When the found expression is a fragment literal and the expected type is `View`, a steer would close the gap: "a fragment `<>…` is a `List`, not one view — wrap its children in an element (`
…
`), or return `List`". Repro: finds/fragment_as_view_return.vl. Sizing XS–S; the mismatch reporter keyed on the fragment's lowering marker.
